item.title: The Collapse of Open Source
item.description:
I still read open source every day. I’ve mostly stopped installing it.

How I build now

When I build something now, I go looking for how other people solved the problem. I read their code. Then I close the tab and have a model write the part I need into my own codebase.

No package. No dependency tree underneath it.

I should say where I stand before going on. I publish open source myself. hexa is MIT-licensed and alpha, one of a lot of tools trying to tame the genie. I’m not arguing against publishing. I’m describing a change in how I consume.

item.title: The Rules Nobody Wrote Down
item.description:
For twenty years, good software depended on people remembering which parts of a program were allowed to talk to which. AI coding tools don’t remember. So the rule has to be written down where a machine can enforce it.

A growing share of new code is written by AI. One peer-reviewed study estimates that by early 2025 about 29 percent of new Python functions pushed to GitHub from the United States were AI-written, the highest rate the study measured, up from about 5 percent in 2022.
